stories.title: 12 parties sign peace pact as IGP warns against election violence
stories.body: Inspector-General of Police Olatunji Disu warned parties and their supporters against violence ahead of the 2027 elections, at a meeting with INEC and party leaders in Abuja. Twelve parties signed a peace agreement to renounce violence and thuggery and to take election disputes to court. INEC chairman Joash Amupitan said presidential and National Assembly elections are set for 16 January 2027, and governorship and state assembly elections for 6 February 2027.
stories.why: Election dates and election security are likely exam and interview topics in the run-up to 2027.

cards.front: When are Nigeria's 2027 presidential and National Assembly elections (INEC)?
cards.back: 16 January 2027. Governorship and state assembly elections follow on 6 February 2027.

stories.title: Putin vows retaliation after Ukraine hits Russian oil refineries
stories.body: President Putin said Ukraine keeps attacking Russian refineries despite President Trump's request to stop, and that Russian retaliation is inevitable. Ukraine says it will stop hitting Russian energy targets only if Russia does the same. Industry sources told Reuters that Ukrainian drones have cut Russian refinery processing by 45 percent since late October; this is unconfirmed. Poland said three Russian missiles landed on its territory, and Ukraine said it sank a Russian corvette in a Libyan port with sea drones.
stories.why: Strikes on energy targets affect world fuel supply, and attacks spilling into NATO's Poland raise the risk of a wider war.

stories.title: US sanctions Iran's 'shadow banking'; Iran calls the blockade aggression
stories.body: The US Treasury sanctioned more than two dozen Iranian exchange houses, front companies and staff it says help Iran move billions of dollars, which Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent called the last financial lifeline of the regime. Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baghaei said the sanctions and naval blockade amount to military aggression and that Iran will use all available means to respond, citing Article 51 of the UN Charter. Iran says Hormuz could reopen within two days if the US lifts the blockade and sanctions.
stories.why: Sanctions and the blockade keep Iranian oil off the market, and the risk of new fighting keeps oil prices high.

cards.front: What does Article 51 of the UN Charter cover?
cards.back: The right of self-defence if a country is attacked.

stories.title: Attack in Niger State's Borgu LGA sparks deadly reprisals
stories.body: Suspected terrorists attacked Lumman-Ba'are and Gada-Oli communities in Borgu LGA, Niger State, at dawn on 21 November. Police confirmed about five deaths; local reports put the toll at 11 or more, including a village head and his family. Kambari militias then attacked Fulani residents and refugees in nearby villages including Wawa, where eyewitnesses counted about 20 bodies. The total death toll is unconfirmed.
stories.why: Revenge attacks along ethnic lines can turn a single terror raid into wider communal violence, a pattern seen across the North-central.

cards.front: Which Niger State LGA saw a terror attack and reprisal killings on 21 November 2026?

stories.title: Kushner says Russia is 'comfortable' with NATO-style guarantees for Ukraine
stories.body: At a Coalition of the Willing meeting in Berlin on 19 November, US envoy Jared Kushner said Russia is comfortable with post-war security guarantees for Ukraine modelled on NATO's Article 5, and that President Trump is open to the idea. President Putin has called NATO membership or NATO guarantees for Ukraine unacceptable. President Zelenskyy said there was no common understanding of what such guarantees would mean, and no details have been agreed.
stories.why: Security guarantees are the main condition Ukraine sets for any ceasefire deal.

cards.back: The collective defence clause: an attack on one member is treated as an attack on all.
